stages.name: Independent
stages.desc: Free of Assyria: pays no regular tribute

stages.name: Tributary vassal
stages.desc: Keeps its own king but pays tribute and obeys Assyria

stages.name: Assyrian province
stages.desc: Ruled directly by an Assyrian governor, including Assyria itself

stages.name: In revolt
stages.desc: Has thrown off Assyrian rule or stopped paying tribute

stages.name: Sacked or destroyed
stages.desc: Stormed, plundered or razed by an army

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: Cypriot kingdoms and the Tyrian colony of Kition
Seven kings of Cyprus submit to Sargon II; his stele stands at Kition
Luli of Tyre takes refuge on the island and dies in exile
Esarhaddon lists ten Cypriot kings among his vassals
No Assyrian record of Cypriot tribute after the 660s

states.name: Israel
timeline: The kingdom of Israel under Omri, building his new capital at Samaria
Ahab of Israel brings two thousand chariots to the coalition at Qarqar
Jehu of Israel bows before Shalmaneser III, as the Black Obelisk shows
Menahem of Israel pays Tiglath-pileser III a thousand talents of silver
Galilee and the coast become the Assyrian province of Megiddo
Samaria falls after a three-year siege; thousands are deported
Samaria becomes the province of Samerina, resettled with deportees
Sennacherib storms Lachish, in Judah's lowlands
Ashurbanipal punishes Akko, hanging its rebels on stakes
Assyrian provinces hold the north and the coast
Assyrian rule fades; Josiah of Judah moves north

states.name: Palestine
timeline: The hill kingdom of Judah and the Philistine city of Gaza
Tiglath-pileser III reaches Gaza; Ahaz of Judah pays tribute
Sargon II defeats Gaza and Egypt at Raphia
Hezekiah of Judah joins Luli and the Philistines in revolt
Sennacherib takes forty-six walled towns; Jerusalem is besieged but not stormed
Hezekiah pays a heavy tribute and keeps his throne
Josiah of Judah stops paying as Assyria weakens

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Tyre, Sidon and Byblos send Ashurnasirpal II silver, gold, purple cloth and ivory
Tyrians ferry tribute to Shalmaneser III by boat, as the Balawat Gates show
Tyre and Sidon pay Shalmaneser III at Mount Ba'li-ra'si
Hiram II of Tyre and Sibitti-bi'li of Byblos pay Tiglath-pileser III
Mattan II of Tyre pays 150 talents of gold; Assyrian agents tax the timber trade
Tyre resists Shalmaneser V, who is said to blockade the island for five years
Tyre submits again under Sargon II
Luli of Tyre and Sidon withholds tribute after Sargon's death
Luli flees to Cyprus; Sennacherib puts Tuba'lu on the throne of Sidon
Abdi-Milkuti of Sidon rebels against Esarhaddon
Esarhaddon takes Sidon, razes it and throws its walls into the sea
Sidon's land becomes the province of Kar-Esarhaddon; Tyre and Byblos remain vassals
Baal I of Tyre sides with Egypt; Esarhaddon blockades the island
Tyre submits to Ashurbanipal; governors hold the mainland coast
Ashurbanipal punishes Ushu, Tyre's mainland town, and Akko for rebellion
Assyrian governors hold the coast of Sidon and Tyre's mainland
As Assyria falters, the cities slip free (the date is uncertain)

states.name: Syria
timeline: Arwad and the northern Aramaean kings pay Ashurnasirpal II
Shalmaneser III annexes Bit-Adini; Til Barsip becomes Kar-Shalmaneser
Damascus, Hamath and Arwad lead the coalition that faces Assyria at Qarqar
Hazael of Damascus holds out against Shalmaneser III
Adad-nirari III takes tribute from Damascus and Arwad
Tiglath-pileser III makes Simirra, on the coast north of Byblos, a province
Damascus falls and becomes an Assyrian province
Yau-bi'di of Hamath raises Arpad, Simirra and Damascus against Sargon II
Sargon crushes the rebels at Qarqar and burns the city
Hamath becomes a province; Arwad keeps its own king as a vassal
Assyrian rule collapses; Egypt and Babylon will contest the land

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Carchemish and Patina pay Ashurnasirpal II; Urartu grows in the east
Tiglath-pileser III routs Sarduri II of Urartu near Arpad
Sargon II annexes Carchemish
Que (Cilicia) and Tabal are made provinces
Sanduarri of Kundu and Sissu, in Cilicia, allies with Sidon
Sanduarri is beheaded; Cilicia is held by Assyrian governors
Assyria's last king, Ashur-uballit II, makes his stand at Harran

states.name: Iraq
timeline: The Assyrian heartland: Ashurnasirpal II rules from his new capital, Kalhu
Sennacherib moves the capital to Nineveh
Sennacherib floods and destroys rebellious Babylon
Babylonia is ruled by Assyrian kings and governors
Babylon rises under Shamash-shum-ukin, Ashurbanipal's brother
Babylon falls after a two-year siege
Nabopolassar takes Babylon's throne; the south breaks away
The Medes sack Ashur, Assyria's oldest city
Medes and Babylonians storm and burn Nineveh

states.name: Jordan
timeline: The kingdoms of Ammon, Moab and Edom
Ammon sends troops to the coalition at Qarqar
Ammon, Moab and Edom pay Tiglath-pileser III
Tribute to Assyria lapses

states.name: Egypt
timeline: Egypt, divided under the Libyan pharaohs
An Egyptian army is beaten at Raphia but Egypt stays free
Esarhaddon's first invasion of Egypt is driven back
Esarhaddon takes Memphis; Taharqa flees south
Taharqa returns and retakes Memphis
Ashurbanipal's army restores Assyrian vassals in the Delta
Tantamani of Kush drives the Assyrians out
Ashurbanipal's army sacks Thebes
Psamtik I of Sais rules as an Assyrian vassal
Psamtik reunites Egypt and quietly stops paying (the date is debated)

states.name: N. Cyprus
timeline: Salamis and the kingdoms of northern Cyprus
The Cypriot kings submit to Sargon II
Kings of Salamis and their neighbours pay Esarhaddon
No Assyrian record of Cypriot tribute after the 660s

events.title: Washing weapons
events.text: Ashurnasirpal II reaches the Mediterranean, washes his weapons in the sea and takes tribute from Tyre, Sidon, Byblos and Arwad (the year is debated).

events.title: Cedars of Lebanon
events.text: Ashurnasirpal cuts cedar on the Amanus and Lebanon for his new palace at Kalhu.

events.title: Palace at Kalhu
events.text: Ashurnasirpal's new palace at Kalhu is lined with reliefs of tribute bearers and burning cities.

events.title: Tribute by boat
events.text: In Shalmaneser III's first year, Tyrians ferry tribute ashore in boats, a scene cast on the Balawat Gates.

events.title: Til Barsip annexed
events.text: Shalmaneser III annexes Bit-Adini and renames its capital Kar-Shalmaneser.

events.title: Battle of Qarqar
events.text: Twelve kings, Ahab and Arwad among them, meet Shalmaneser III; both sides claim victory.

events.title: Jehu's tribute
events.text: Jehu of Israel kneels before Shalmaneser III on the Black Obelisk; Tyre and Sidon also pay.

events.title: Ba'li-ra'si
events.text: Shalmaneser III takes tribute of Tyre and Sidon on a headland by the sea, probably Mount Carmel.

events.title: Sailing west
events.text: By tradition Tyre founds Carthage; some scholars link the push west to Assyria's demand for silver.

events.title: Dur-Sharrukin
events.text: Sargon II begins a new capital whose reliefs show Phoenician ships towing cedar logs.

events.title: Adad-nirari's tribute
events.text: Adad-nirari III takes tribute from Damascus, Tyre and Sidon.

events.title: Urartu routed
events.text: Tiglath-pileser III defeats Sarduri II of Urartu near Arpad.

events.title: Hiram's tribute
events.text: Hiram II of Tyre, Menahem of Israel and Rezin of Damascus pay Tiglath-pileser III.

events.title: Province of Simirra
events.text: The coast north of Byblos becomes the Assyrian province of Simirra.

events.title: March to Gaza
events.text: Tiglath-pileser III marches down the coast to Gaza; Hanunu flees to Egypt.

events.title: Damascus falls
events.text: Tiglath-pileser III takes Damascus, kills King Rezin and deports its people.

events.title: Taxing the timber
events.text: Assyrian officials post customs men at Tyre and Sidon and ban timber sales to Egypt.

events.title: Siege of Tyre
events.text: Shalmaneser V blockades island Tyre, a siege known only from a later Greek source.

events.title: Samaria falls
events.text: Shalmaneser V and Sargon II both claim Samaria; its people are deported.

events.title: Qarqar burned
events.text: Sargon II crushes the revolt of Hamath and its allies and burns Qarqar.

events.title: Raphia
events.text: Sargon II defeats Gaza and an Egyptian army on the border of Egypt.

events.title: Carchemish annexed
events.text: Sargon II deports the king of Carchemish and annexes the city.

events.title: Kition stele
events.text: Seven kings of Cyprus submit; Sargon II's stele is set up at Kition.

events.title: Nineveh rebuilt
events.text: Sennacherib makes Nineveh his capital and builds his Palace without Rival.

events.title: Luli's flight
events.text: Luli, king of Tyre and Sidon, flees by sea to Cyprus; a Nineveh relief shows the escape.

events.title: Lachish stormed
events.text: Sennacherib storms Lachish and later lines a palace room with reliefs of the siege.

events.title: Jerusalem besieged
events.text: Hezekiah is shut in 'like a bird in a cage', but the city is not taken.

events.title: Babylon destroyed
events.text: Sennacherib floods and razes rebellious Babylon.

events.title: Sidon razed
events.text: Esarhaddon takes Sidon, tears down its walls and deports its people.

events.title: Two heads
events.text: The heads of Abdi-Milkuti and Sanduarri of Cilicia are paraded through Nineveh.

events.title: Kar-Esarhaddon
events.text: A new Assyrian harbour town is built on Sidon's coast.

events.title: Treaty with Tyre
events.text: Esarhaddon binds Baal I of Tyre by a treaty that controls his ports and ships.

events.title: Ten kings of Cyprus
events.text: Esarhaddon's prism lists ten Cypriot kings who sent building materials.

events.title: Memphis taken
events.text: Esarhaddon takes Memphis; Tyre, allied with Egypt, is blockaded.

events.title: Thebes sacked
events.text: Ashurbanipal's army sacks Thebes, Egypt's holy city.

events.title: Tyre submits
events.text: Ashurbanipal blockades Tyre; Baal I sends his daughter and his son Yahimilki.

events.title: Arwad's king
events.text: Yakinlu of Arwad submits; after his death Ashurbanipal picks his successor.

events.title: Brothers' war
events.text: Shamash-shum-ukin, king of Babylon, rebels against his brother Ashurbanipal.

events.title: Ushu and Akko
events.text: Ashurbanipal punishes Tyre's mainland town and Akko for rebellion.

events.title: Nabopolassar
events.text: Nabopolassar becomes king of Babylon and begins the war against Assyria.

events.title: Ashur sacked
events.text: The Medes sack Ashur, Assyria's ancient religious capital.

events.title: Nineveh falls
events.text: Medes and Babylonians storm Nineveh; the empire's capital is burned.

events.title: Stand at Harran
events.text: Ashur-uballit II makes Harran Assyria's last capital.

chartNote: Share of the area of today's ten countries and territories on the map, by their relationship to Assyria. Regions are modern boundaries; each takes the status of its leading city or kingdom (Lebanon follows Tyre and Sidon, Syria its Aramaean kingdoms and Arwad, Turkey its southern rim), a simplification. Large Egypt and Turkey swing the shares. Many dates are disputed by a year or more.
